recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source edit is needed unless FHIR-I later chooses to define portable modifier semantics for chained or reverse-chained search.
issue_request: FHIR-26886 was a Published/Not Persuasive with Modification FHIR-I R4 issue asking how modifiers such as :not should work in reverse chaining, for example Patient?_has:Condition:patient:code:not=X,Y,Z. The resolution requested notes in the Chaining and Reverse Chaining sections that forward and reverse chaining are not intended to support modifiers, with _filter as an alternative.
initial_application: The issue was applied by commit 1750a1f28827a057685c0b8150320636ebc5e7e9, which added modifier guidance to source/search.html under both #chaining and #has. A later FHIR-45252 reconciliation reorganized the forward-chaining note into a list while preserving its substance.
additional_context: source/search.html is active build source through publish.ini. Earlier FHIR-12068 removed explicit _has limitations including a modifier prohibition, so the current non-prohibitive warning is consistent with that history. FHIR-13324 separately explains that flat URL search cannot express some grouped chained/_has joins and points complex cases to _filter or composites. The 2020-05-11 FHIR-I minutes record the FHIR-26886 motion, and the originating Zulip discussion confirms the spec ambiguity.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source has the forward-chaining modifier note at source/search.html:4506-4508 and the reverse-chaining modifier note at source/search.html:4573-4576, with links to Named Queries and Advanced filtering.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Published _has issue removed explicit restrictions including a modifier prohibition, which supports preserving FHIR-26886 as cautionary non-prohibitive guidance.
Resolved - No Change issue for grouped _has AND semantics explains the flat URL syntax limitation and recommends _filter or composite parameters for complex cases.
Later Search page reconciliation reorganized the forward-chaining note but preserved the FHIR-26886 guidance.
